name: PaywallProject
author: PaywallProject

sections.description:
PaywallProject helps publishers sell access to protected content with Stripe-powered subscriptions, gifts, coupons, subscriber management, and reporting.

Learn more, read the documentation and get support at paywallproject.com.

Payments and fees

Payments go through Connect with Stripe. Connect your Stripe account in one click, with no API keys or webhooks to set up. PaywallProject charges a platform fee of 10% on each payment, on top of Stripe’s own fees. The fee is shown on the Connect button before you agree to it.

Gift articles

Let subscribers share single stories with people who don’t subscribe. Turn it on per level under Levels → Gift articles and set how many gifts each subscriber gets a month. Each gift is a link that unlocks one article for one reader, once, and expires after 72 hours. A level gifts every article by default. You can limit it to some categories, or allow every category except some. A category includes its subcategories. When a level is limited to some categories, posts with no category can’t be gifted. When it allows every category except some, posts with no category can be gifted, and so can post types without categories. Gift links already sent keep working until they expire, even if you change the categories.

AI Shield

Keep AI companies from crawling your stories while Google, Bing and other search engines index your site as before. Turn it on under Settings → AI Shield and PaywallProject adds a rule for each AI crawler to your robots.txt — training crawlers such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot and CCBot, and AI search and assistant fetchers such as ChatGPT-User and PerplexityBot. robots.txt only stops crawlers that respect it, so the tab also gives you a ready-to-copy Cloudflare WAF rule that blocks the same crawlers at the edge, which works even when your pages are served from a full-page cache. Untick any crawler you want to let in. Googlebot, Bingbot, Applebot and DuckDuckBot are never blocked. Off by default.

AI and MCP

Connect your staff’s MCP client to your own site to read subscriber data and run support actions. MCP needs WordPress 6.9 or newer and the separate MCP Adapter plugin. Tested with MCP Adapter 0.7.1. Each staff member connects with an Application Password and the permissions of their WordPress account. Write tools allow 30 attempts per minute per Application Password. Read tools do not use the write allowance.

Open PaywallProject → Settings → AI and MCP to set it up in three steps: install the MCP Adapter with one click, connect, and copy the ready-made setup for Claude Code, Cursor, or Claude Desktop. A Test connection button checks it works. Support staff connect from their own Profile page. The bundled MCP connection guide covers manual setup.

External services

This plugin connects to the third-party services below. Nothing is sent to a service until you configure it.

Stripe

Stripe processes all payments. The plugin calls the Stripe API (api.stripe.com) when a reader checks out, buys a gift, changes or cancels a subscription, when tax is calculated at checkout, and when an administrator manages subscribers or coupons. It sends the reader’s email address, name, billing and shipping address, the plan and price, and for tax estimates without an address, the reader’s IP address. Checkout pages load Stripe.js from js.stripe.com, which collects card details directly; card numbers never reach your site.

  • Terms: https://stripe.com/legal/ssa
  • Privacy: https://stripe.com/privacy

PaywallProject Connect hub (paywallproject.com)

Used for all payments made through Connect with Stripe. Before you connect, the plugin asks the hub for the platform fee rate and sends your site URL. When you connect, disconnect, or refresh the connection, it sends your site URL and the connection credentials. While connected, every Stripe API request listed above goes through the hub (https://paywallproject.com/wp-json/ppconnect/v1), which forwards it to Stripe and applies the platform fee. That includes the reader data listed under Stripe.

  • Terms: https://www.paywallproject.com/terms-of-service/
  • Privacy policy: https://www.paywallproject.com/privacy-policy/

Google reCAPTCHA

Used only when reCAPTCHA is selected as the signup protection. Registration and checkout forms load the reCAPTCHA script from google.com, which collects data about the visitor’s browser. When a form is submitted, the plugin sends the captcha token, your secret key and the visitor’s IP address to Google to verify it.

  • Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms
  • Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Cloudflare Turnstile

Used only when Turnstile is selected as the signup protection. Registration and checkout forms load the Turnstile script from challenges.cloudflare.com. When a form is submitted, the plugin sends the Turnstile token, your secret key and the visitor’s IP address to Cloudflare to verify it.

  • Terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/
  • Privacy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/

Slack

Used only when you enter a Slack webhook URL. When a subscriber signs up, renews or cancels, the plugin posts a message with the subscriber’s email address and plan to that webhook.

  • Terms: https://slack.com/terms-of-service
  • Privacy: https://slack.com/trust/privacy/privacy-policy

Outgoing webhooks (Zapier and others)

Used only when you add a webhook URL. On the subscriber events you select, the plugin posts the event name and subscriber details (email address, name, plan and status) to the URL you entered. The data goes to whichever service owns that URL, under that service’s terms.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/paywallproject directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to PaywallProject, choose Connect with Stripe, and set up your access settings.
sections.faq:
Does this require Stripe?

Yes. Stripe is the supported payment gateway for this version.

Is there a fee?

Yes. PaywallProject takes a platform fee of 10% of each payment made through Connect with Stripe. Stripe’s own fees apply as well.

Where can I get help?

Visit paywallproject.com for guides and support, or post in the plugin’s support forum here on WordPress.org.
sections.changelog:
4.1.0

  • Feature: Connect AI assistants over MCP — set it up in one click (installs the MCP Adapter, connects, copies the config and tests it), then let Claude or another assistant look up and manage subscribers, subscriptions, levels, coupons, groups, gifts, post access, settings and emails, with a write limit and an audit log of every change.
  • Feature: Refund a Stripe charge from the transaction page — in full or in part, with a required reason and a preview of the amount before it goes through.
  • Feature: Staff can cancel, resume, reactivate and change a reader’s plan from wp-admin, with a price preview first; partial refunds now show as partially refunded.
  • Feature: Abandoned-checkout reminders — readers who leave checkout, even before an account exists, get reminder emails that can each carry their own coupon and a secure link back to their checkout. A reader is only reminded when Stripe shows they never paid.
  • Feature: Protect e-edition PDFs and dFlip flipbooks behind the paywall, or protect a single PDF from the media library. Refused readers see an on-brand access page whose wording, links and cover you can edit.
  • Feature: A level can limit gift articles to some categories, or to all categories except some.
  • Improvement: Reconcile with Stripe now also fixes subscribers whose Stripe subscription has ended, pages through large Stripe accounts and skips lifetime levels.
  • Improvement: A reader who enters an existing account’s email at checkout now gets a sign-in step right under the email field, with sign-in attempts throttled.
  • Improvement: The abandoned-checkout notice is hidden by default, with a setting to show it.
  • Improvement: The email editor says who gets each template, and when.
  • Improvement: New wordpress.org banner.

4.0.1

  • Security: Hardened the 3-D Secure checkout finalization.
  • Security: Hardened how REST requests from logged-in members are authenticated.
  • Security: Removed the endpoint that revealed whether an email address has an account, and finishing a free signup now requires the verified one-time code.
  • Security: Every public route, admin form and database query is now checked, sanitized, prepared and escaped, following the WordPress.org plugin review.
  • Fix: The Newsletter Glue “Sync all subscribers” button in Tools no longer crashes.

Older releases are listed in changelog.txt.
